messages:
anika: Heads-up, onboarding q4-int8 to OCR->translate vertical pipeline produced odd token duplication and occasional sentence reordering around ideographic line breaks. BLEU drop ~5.9 on hk-vertical-smoke. :confused:

mei: Can you share a minimal repro and metric delta?

anika: Small repro comparing fp16 baseline -> q4-int8 (staging):
```
input: "\n2"  # (actually: three short Han lines; trimmed here)
baseline: "Line A. Line B."
q4-int8: "Line A. Line A. Line B."  # duplication of first line mid-output
```
BLEU baseline 32.0 -> q4-int8 26.1 (hk-vertical-smoke, n=1.9k). EM-like drop ~13%.

dmitri: Duplication + reorder sounds like a KV-cache/segment boundary bug in the quantized merge kernels. Any tokenizer/detok traces?

anika: I attached tokenizer trace snippet: token ids around boundary: [198, 0xFEFF, 198, 0x0A, 199]. Only shows up on q4-int8. Raw bytes near break: e4 b8 96 e3 80 82 0a e4 b8 97.

mei: FEFF (BOM) insertion is suspicious; maybe a masking bug where a zeroed cache slot gets promoted to a visible codepoint after int8 rounding in the merge op. Can you repro with --deterministic-cache to rule out race?

anika: Repro steps I used:
1) image: redwood/q4-int8:2026-03-24-staging
2) run: ./repro.sh --dataset hk-vertical-smoke --num 200 --trace-detok > q4_repro.log
3) compare with redwood/q4-fp16:stable
Result: deterministic-cache flag restores baseline behavior (BLEU 31.7).

dmitri: Good signal. I'll bisect the int8 merge op changes and check the cache zeroing/path where we memcpy pre-merged spans. If zero bytes get interpreted as FEFF after quant conversion that's our bug.

build-bot: Canary alert: q4-int8 (canary-4) detok-smoke FAILED (delta BLEU -5.9). Rolling back canary and notifying owners.

mei: Short-term mitigation: disable aggressive int8 cache packing on vertical-locales, and add a CI detok roundtrip for hk-vertical-smoke + ja-vertical to catch regressions.

anika: Added 50 failing excerpts + full repro log to the issue. Link: https://priv.redwood/issue/ML-4521 (internal).

dmitri: I'll open PR with two things: 1) fix zeroing in pack_cache() and 2) unit test that fuzzes linebreak adjacent merges under int8 kernels. If tests pass, we can re-enable packing for a limited canary.

mei: Also add a small end-to-end eval in qa-bot that runs the hk-vertical-smoke subset on any runtime kernel change; mark as required for canary promotion.

anika: TL;DR: q4-int8 merge/pack cache bug causes duplicated first-line emission on vertical Han OCR inputs; workaround: disable aggressive cache packing and gate canary until pack fix + tests.
